newsitem.title: JORDAN: Foreign buying propels Amman shares to new highs.
newsitem.headline: Foreign buying propels Amman shares to new highs.

text.p: Jordan's stock market surged on Sunday to its highest level in nearly two years fueled by undiminished global fund appetite for blue chips, dealers said.

The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 1.59 points to 164.35 points in strong trade worth 4.5 million dinars ($8.8 million) dominated by emerging fund buying on a handful of mining and bank stocks.
Nearly a third of trade was in Jordan Cement shares, which rose another 0.12 dinar to close at 4.41 dinars with over 329,610 shares changing hands in deals worth 1.45 million dinars..
Jordan's top export earners Arab Potash and Jordan Phosphates were also popular with emerging funds.

"Movement of prices was still reasonable considering the P/E ratios of blue chips," said Samir Jaradat, head of investments at Jordan Investment Finance Bank, who executes orders on behalf of foreigners.
But in a warning about current price levels, Jaradat said "international fund buyers were very price-conscious when prices are too high or too low."

Supply of the popular blue chips was again generated by institutional investors ready to sell part of their portfolios after prices shot up as much as eight percent since the outside funds began stepping up their purchases two weeks ago.

But investment analysts said sustained foreign buying needed large institutional investors such as the government social security corporation and its investment arm to start long delayed sell-offs of their vast stock portfolio.
The market is hampered by a shortage of the blue chip shares most in demand by funds because many have already reached a 50 percent ceiling on foreign ownership.

In banks, Jordan National Bank saw the heaviest buying orders after Jordan Cement, a factor that helped it rise by the five percent daily price ceiling limit to 2.27 dinars in trade worth 756,725 dinars.

But Housing Bank, which rose 0.07 dinar to 5.19 dinars, saw a lull in the heavy foreign demand it generated on Saturday, with only 327,683 dinars worth of trade compared to over one million dinars of trade that day.

Other blue chips attracting notice on a smaller scale were Jordan's Petroleum Refinery, which rose 0.06 dinar to 10.01 dinars along with Dar al-Dawa, which rose 4.17 percent to 5.50 dinars in trade worth 197,476 dinars.
Overall advancing shares outnumbered losers 25 to sixteen, while another seventeen closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.39 percent to 82.15 points, down 1.49 percent from the start of the year.
